question.problem: Find the radius of curvature for the curve $r(t)={t}^{2}\,i+({t}^{2}-t)\,j$ at $t=0.$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{|{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)|}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

The radius of curvature $R$ is defined as
$R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}.$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)={t}^{2},\,y(t)={t}^{2}-t.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =2t,\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =2t-1 \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =2,\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{|2t\cdot 2-(2t-1)\cdot 2|}{{((2t)^{2}+(2t-1)^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{(8{t}^{2}-4t+1)}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(0) & =\frac{2}{{(8(0)^{2}-4(0)+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{(0-0+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{1}{κ(0)}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
